d: Learn how to add visual effects to your games.
h:
You can create special effects by parenting special effect objects to other objects or attachments.

Light sources

Light sources let you attach lighting effects to objects or attachments. There are three types of light sources:

  • A PointLight emits light spherically from a single point. This object is ideal for non-directional lights like bulbs, torches, and fireballs.
  • A SpotLight emits light in the shape of a cone with a spherical base. This object is ideal for directional lights like street lamps, flashlights, and headlights.
  • A SurfaceLight emits light from the face of a BasePart. This object is ideal for lighting from TV or computer screens, billboards, and fluorescent panels.

Particle emitters

A particle emitter is an object that emits customizable 2D images (particles) into the world, useful for simulating special effects like fire, smoke, and sparks.

Beams

A beam is an object that renders a texture between two Attachment objects Beam.Attachment0 and Beam.Attachment1. By setting beam properties, you can:

  • Add a texture and color gradient to create interesting visuals like waterfalls and force fields.
  • Modify a beam's transparency so that it fades over time.
  • Warp its shape by changing the width or curve of each attachment point.

Trails

A trail is an object that creates a trail between and behind two Attachment objects as they move through space. Trails can help players visualize movement, such as a sword slashing through the air, projectiles flying to their target, or footprints walking away.

By setting trail properties, you can:

  • Add a texture to create interesting visuals.
  • Set a constant or gradient color.
  • Modify a trail's lifetime.

Highlighting

Highlight is a visual effect which you can use to call attention to a specific object within a game, such as to provide visual feedback that the object is important and/or interactable. See Highlighting Objects for details.

kid.simple: This page is a quick tour of the special effects you can add to a Roblox game. You make most effects by putting an effect object inside a part or an attachment. There are lights, particle emitters (fire, smoke, sparks), beams (lasers, waterfalls), trails (sword swooshes), and highlights (glowing outlines). Each one has its own page with more detail.
kid.analogy: Think of effects like stickers and glow sticks for your build: the part is the toy, and you stick an effect onto it to make it shine, sparkle, or leave a streak.
keyPoints: You create effects by parenting an effect object to a part or an attachment.
There are three light types: `PointLight` (glows in every direction, like a bulb or torch), `SpotLight` (a cone, like a flashlight), and `SurfaceLight` (glows from one face, like a TV screen).
A `ParticleEmitter` shoots out lots of small 2D images to make fire, smoke, sparks, and more.
A `Beam` draws a texture between two attachments. You can change its color, fade, width, and curve for things like waterfalls and force fields.
A `Trail` draws a streak behind two moving attachments, great for sword slashes, flying projectiles, or footprints.
A `Highlight` puts an outline and colored overlay on an object to show it is important or can be used.

terms.parent / parenting: Putting one object inside another in the Explorer. If a light is inside a part, the part is its parent and the light glows from that part.
terms.attachment: An invisible point inside a part. Effects like beams and trails need attachments to know where to start and end.
terms.particle: One tiny flat picture, like a single spark or puff of smoke. Emitters make lots of them.
terms.texture: An image used to paint the look of an effect, like a laser pattern on a beam.
terms.gradient: A smooth change from one color or value to another, like red fading into yellow.

watchOut: Beams and trails need two attachments. Without both, nothing shows up.
Too many particles or very big ones can make the game slow, especially on phones. Start small.
Effects are visual only. A glowing beam will not hurt players unless you also write a script for it.
